name: FORM — EUCL (Euclidean) machine
convention: key 0 = AUX; keys 1-10 = black keys (top row); keys 11-26 = white keys (16-step row, key 11 = step 0). '#000000' = off. EUCL does NOT consume the whole grid: the container keeps painting the top-row machine picker, and EUCL paints only the lower 16 step keys.
notes: EUCL is the second FORM machine: a Euclidean rhythm generator (events distributed over steps with rotation, one note per hit). Step-row legend: ORANGE #ff8000 = a hit, LOWWHITE #202020 = a rest, WHITE #ffffff = the playhead, off = beyond the pattern's step count. Params are edited with the encoder over two pages — RHYTHM (Steps / Hits / Rotation / Note) and NOTE (Vel / Chan / Length / Swing). Tapping a step key rotates the pattern so it starts on that step. Top row stays as the container machine picker (selected EUCL slot = WHITE, other EUCL = CYAN, OMNI = ORANGE).

states.name: EUCL — E(5,16) playing
states.notes: A 16-step Euclidean pattern with 5 hits, rotation 0 (hits on steps 0,3,6,10,13). Top row: key3=selected EUCL=WHITE, key4=OMNI=ORANGE, key5=EUCL=CYAN. Step row: ORANGE=hit, LOWWHITE=rest, and the WHITE playhead is on step 6 (key17, a hit). Encoder RHYTHM page edits Steps/Hits/Rotation/Note.

encoder.note: Turn = select param (Steps/Hits/Rotation/Note...); AUX+turn or press+turn = edit

states.name: EUCL — E(4,12), steps < 16
states.notes: Pattern shortened to 12 steps with 4 hits (steps 0,3,6,9). Because Steps=12, keys 23-26 (steps 12-15) fall beyond the pattern and go dark — this is how a shorter Euclidean length reads on the grid. Playhead shown on step 3 (key14, a hit).

keyNotes.23: Step 12 — beyond the 12-step length, so off

encoder.note: Turn = select param; AUX+turn = edit. NOTE page: Vel/Chan/Length/Swing
